Tiny motes of golden fae-light drifting lazily between the trunks, brightest where the shadows pool, like the forest breathing softly glowing dust.
Fireflies weaving slow constellations above the grass and the water, their tiny lights doubling in the glassy reflection below.
Luminous waist-high mist lying across the clearing, glowing pearl where the light touches it, the flowers rising through it like small islands.
Blossom petals drifting like slow snow from the canopy, each catching the light as it turns, a few settling on the water's skin.
Golden pollen haze hanging in the shafts of afternoon light, shimmering faintly, as though the air itself has been dusted with something warm.
Dandelion seeds floating upward through a beam of sun, lit from behind so each one glows like a tiny held breath.
A faint shimmer hovering just above the pond's surface, as though the water remembers last night's moonlight and cannot quite let it go.
Woodsmoke curling from the cottage chimney in a slow soft ribbon, catching the light before it dissolves into the canopy above.
Dew still hanging suspended in the air where mist has just lifted, each droplet catching the morning light like a briefly held jewel.
Slow falling leaves turning one by one through a long shaft of light, amber and gold, descending as though time has been gently slowed.
Thin luminous fog threading between the trunks at knee height, pale and quietly glowing, parting softly around anything that moves through it.
Soft glowing spores drifting from the mossy boughs overhead, unhurried, each one faintly luminous in the green-filtered shade beneath the trees.
A warm golden haze settling over the cottage garden just before evening, too still to be dust, too soft to be anything ordinary.
Silvery threads of spider-silk catching the afternoon light between branches, strung like the faintest possible attempt at decoration no one planned.
The air above the stream holding a faint iridescence where sunlight meets the mist rising off the water, barely there, quietly lovely.
Pale seed-down from the meadow grasses drifting through the clearing in loose slow clusters, lit golden where they pass through open light.
A soft luminous breath rising from the moss after rain, not quite mist, not quite steam, just the earth exhaling something gentle and warm.
Floating fragments of lichen, impossibly light, turning slowly through a beam of late sun as though they have nowhere particular to be.
The late afternoon light thickening to amber between the trees, the air itself seeming to glow faintly from no single direction at once.
Tiny bright specks of reflected light scattered across the path where the stream catches the sun and throws it through the leaves.
A drift of pale feathers from some unseen bird settling slowly through the canopy light, each one rotating as it descends through the green.
Mist pooling softly in the low hollows of the garden, glowing faintly blue-white in the early morning before the sun has fully arrived.
The air between the old trees holding a barely-visible shimmer, the kind that makes you wonder if you have simply been looking too long.
Soft luminous condensation on the meadow grasses just after sunrise, each blade beaded with light, the whole field quietly gleaming in the stillness.
A slow turning column of golden dust motes rising through a gap in the canopy, unhurried and self-contained, like a secret the light is keeping.
